title: Palace: Keeping streets clean post-ASEAN not government's job alone
summary: Palace Press Officer Claire Castro urged Filipinos to practice proper trash disposal and help maintain cleanliness after the regional gathering.

blocks.text: President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. hands over the ceremonial wooden gavel to Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong, marking the transfer of the ASEAN chairmanship on November 17, 2026.

MANILA, Philippines — Filipinos must also do their part to keep the streets clean after the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit, Palace Press Officer Claire Castro said in an interview with DZRH on Wednesday, November 18.

"Madalas naman nagki-clearing din ang Metropolitan Manila Development Authority, 'di ba? Kaya lang syempre 'pag nag-clearing ka, may magtatakbuhang mga illegal vendors. 'Pag may nangyari, ikaw na naman ang sisisihin. Ang paglilinis ng Pilipinas ay hindi lang sa gobyerno," Castro said.

(The Metropolitan Manila Development Authority often conducts clearing operations, doesn't it? But when you conduct clearing operations, some illegal vendors run away. If something happens, you get blamed again. Keeping the Philippines clean is not solely the government's responsibility.)
Her remarks came after cleanup and clearing operations for the 49th ASEAN Summit drew criticism, including allegations that the government was attempting to conceal poverty from visiting delegates.
Large fences and barriers featuring artworks by Filipino National Artists were installed along key motorcade routes in Pasay City.
Rep. Antonio Tinio (ACT Teachers party-list) alleged that the barriers were intended to hide poor communities from visiting delegates.
Some street vendors along these routes were also ordered to temporarily close their stalls for the duration of the summit.

The preparations have also drawn scrutiny over the P22.9 billion allocated for the Philippines' ASEAN hosting activities in 2026. Malacañang previously said the amount covers the country's yearlong chairmanship and related events, not just the November summit.
Castro reiterated the importance of personal responsibility in keeping the country clean, particularly through proper trash disposal.
"Sabi nila, 'Kaya niyo na mag-abroad pero 'yong magtapon ng basura sa tamang basurahan, hindi niyo magawa ... Dito lang napakadaming reklamo.'"
(They say, "You can afford to travel abroad, but you can't even throw your trash in the proper bin ... There are just so many complaints here.")
The 49th ASEAN Summit officially concluded on Tuesday, November 17, with the Philippines formally handing over the ASEAN chairmanship to Singapore for 2027.
Related engagements, including US President Donald Trump's visit, continued on November 18.
